knowledgePattern: Split a floor-function integral into rectangles and combine logarithms

hints.title: Find where the function changes value
hints.body: Use the supplied floor definition to find intervals on which its input has a fixed integer part.
hints.recap: A case-defined function must be evaluated on the inputs covered by each case.
hints.pitfall: The scale inside the floor changes the widths of its constant steps.
hints.pause: Write the first and last constant intervals carefully.

recall.reminder: A case-defined function must be evaluated on the inputs covered by each case.

hints.title: Add the constant strips
hints.body: Write the forward integral as a sum of rectangle widths times their constant heights; keep track of the original direction of integration.
hints.recap: Reversing limits changes the sign of a signed integral.
hints.pitfall: An isolated endpoint value does not contribute a rectangle of positive width.
hints.pause: Express the integral as a finite sum with correct limits and width.

recall.reminder: Reversing limits changes the sign of a signed integral.

hints.title: Combine the logarithms
hints.body: Turn the sum of logarithms into one logarithm of a product, and inspect adjacent factors.
hints.recap: The sum of logarithms of positive quantities is the logarithm of their product.
hints.pitfall: Keep the rectangle width outside the sum and retain all surviving boundary factors.
hints.pause: Simplify the product, evaluate the logarithm and restore the original orientation.

recall.reminder: The sum of logarithms of positive quantities is the logarithm of their product.

solution:
1. Reverse the limits first: the required value is the negative of the integral from 1 to 100.

2. On k/2≤x<(k+1)/2, ⌊2x⌋=k. The relevant integers are k=2,3,…,199, and every interval has width 1/2. The value at the single endpoint 100 does not change the integral.

3. The forward integral is 12∑k=2199log10(k/(k+1))=12log10(2334⋯199200)=12log10(1/100)=−1.

4. Reversing the limits therefore gives 1. Answer F.
